content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working on building an interface to schedule the on and off times for a pump using [product_name] Web Server. I want to add a feature so users can set the start time for a weekly timer. What’s the best approach?

I've attached a simple example. You are probably familiar with retrieving block parameters via VM assignment in VM memory of [product_name]. For the web editor, you'll need to include two analog values for each switching time (on/off) — one for hours, one for minutes. Make sure their display format is set to HEX.
Thank you, that resolved my issue.
Hello, I am building on this for boiler control. You have configured a calendar in the web editor, but I'm unsure how to link it in [product_name] Soft. I can't seem to bind a VM to a weekly timer.
There's an example attached showing the weekly timer and one channel. In [product_name] Soft, check out Parameter-VM-Mapping.
Thank you, I’m starting to understand how it operates now.
How do you apply this method for channels 2 and 3?
It works the same way as for channel 1, you just need to use different addresses.
Hello. What is the process to read the weekly timer value from the web server?
Refer to my earlier post from 5/3/2020 at 3:30 PM. There's an example available for download.

Hi. The example for setting times on the web page worked, and the time updates in [product_name] as expected. However, after a few seconds, the new time reverts on the web page, though the value in [product_name] stays correct. Weekly scheduling for days works reliably. The software versions used are LWE [version_no], LSC [version_no], and [product_name] at [version_no]. Is this a setting issue?
No, that isn’t a settings issue. Without both your current web editor project and the [product_name] program, I can’t give more specific advice.

Please check my earlier post again. I used your project unchanged, except your example was created with LWE [version_no]. On load, it prompts a conversion to [version_no]. Even after starting a new project, it behaves the same. I’ll contact support; this appears unrelated to your work.
Here’s an attempt I made after testing your project. The data is present, but the value box only shows a '16#' descriptor.

I re-read your post. You mentioned that every few seconds the web server values change, but they remain stable in [product_name]. If the web server refreshes values every 2-3 seconds, it’s not actually a web server fault. My project is from an earlier version created with LWE [version_no], prior to [version_no]. Loading older projects in newer versions results in automatic conversion, which is standard. There was no mention of the '16#' notation before — that’s due to the web editor. I've previously opened a topic on removing the '16#' mark when displaying switch times for timers in the extended web server. In LWE [version_no], use the 'Scaled Time' feature, which now has more configuration options. I've attached an example integrating this feature.

I see where the misunderstanding occurred. Your project’s text boxes were just small enough to hide the '#' notation; I noticed it only after resizing them. The support team responded quickly, and I realized I missed mentioning that in my description. Sorry for the confusion and thank you — it’s resolved now. I've also tested your alternate approach using Scaled Time and found it more user-friendly for data entry. Thanks again!

analysis.insight_summary: Users are working on making time-scheduling interfaces for pumps and boilers using [product_name] web tools. Their goal is to let users set and monitor weekly timer values online. Early obstacles involve mapping parameters and tying interface elements to timer controls in [product_name] Soft. They seek help on how to extend scheduling to multiple channels and read timer states remotely. Challenges also include understanding parameter-VM mapping and making connections between web controls and underlying timer logic. There are concerns over usability and the clarity of documentation, particularly with recent and older software versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope for a straightforward way to configure and monitor weekly timer schedules through the web interface. They prefer easy-to-follow instructions or built-in functions for linking web elements to timer logic across multiple channels and reading timer status, minimizing complicated set-up.
